newsitem.title: INDIA: Cyclone ploughs toward India's Andhra Pradesh.
newsitem.headline: Cyclone ploughs toward India's Andhra Pradesh.

text.p: A cyclone threatening the battered southeast Indian state of Andhra Pradesh will hit early on Wednesday if it holds its course and speed, India's meteorological department said on Monday.
Andhra Pradesh is still counting its dead from a storm last month.

"It is likely to intensify further and move in a west-northwesterly direction and cross the Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Kakinada by the early morning of December 4," the department said in a cyclone warning bulletin.
The bulletin said the cyclone was 600 km (375 miles) east-southeast of Machilapatnam on the Andhra Pradesh coast at 2.30 p.m. (0900 GMT) on Monday.
Gale force winds of 70-90 kmph (44-55 mph) and very high seas were expected along Andhra Pradesh's coast on Monday evening, and thunderstorms were expected in neighbouring southern Orissa.
The warning covers hundreds of kilometres of Andhra Pradesh's flat coastline, including the Godavari districts devastated by last month's cyclone.

Cyclone warnings have been sounded in low-lying areas, fishermen have been warned not to put to sea and people in vulnerable areas were being evacuated, a senior state official in the Andhra Pradesh capital Hyderabad said.
The armed forces had been alerted, as had transport departments and medical teams, he said.
More than 2,000 people were either killed or lost at sea after a cyclone hit the same state last month.
